conflict_resolutions.WHOLE_END_ACTOR_DISAGREEMENT: EO 14148 section 2 and EO 14168 section 7(b) are both express rescissions of this order dated 2025-01-20. Neither gives an earlier date, so the first end is 2025-01-20 whichever actor is named; EO 14148 is recorded as the end actor and EO 14168 as a concurrent rescission in the source notes.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held registered text of Executive Order 14021 is the official Federal Register text layer at 86 FR 13803, PDF pages 1-2 (Federal Register / Vol. 86, No. 46 / Thursday, March 11, 2021); it names Executive Order 14021 of March 8, 2021, Guaranteeing an Educational Environment Free From Discrimination on the Basis of Sex, Including Sexual Orientation or Gender Identity, and runs from the title to the signature block. The complete clause inventory was checked against the numbered section headings of that text. Section 2(cc) of Executive Order 14148 of January 20, 2025 (Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions, 90 FR 8237, Federal Register of January 28, 2025) lists Executive Order 14021 of March 8, 2021 among the executive actions that section 2 declares hereby revoked. The held text of Executive Order 14148 states no effective date later than its signing, so the revocation operates from its signing date, 2025-01-20. Whole-order revocation by name is the first end of every clause that had not already been exhausted by performance. The order has no other ending instrument before 2025-01-20 in the packet's later-event chain, which for this order lists besides Executive Order 14148: Executive Order 14168. Each such instrument is recorded in the source notes with its date and why it is not an earlier end; none reinstates this order. Executive Order 14168 section 7(b), signed on the same day, 2025-01-20, is a concurrent express rescission of this order and is not earlier than Executive Order 14148 section 2. The packet's name search of held order texts for this order's number returned, among texts dated on or after 2025-01-20, only Executive Order 14148 and Executive Order 14168. The later-source search is recorded by the three machine searches selected on the sheet: the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09), the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with the CFR bulk files, and the Federal Register executive-order disposition catalog; their coverage statements were read and each is marked complete. Savings are addressed in the savings statement. The first end of the whole order is 2025-01-20.

No earlier revocation, supersession or amendment that ends a clause is shown in the packet's later-event chain; the instruments it lists other than Executive Order 14148 are addressed in the source notes (Executive Order 14168 section 7(b) is a concurrent express rescission dated 2025-01-20).","independent_command_check":"Every clause recorded for Executive Order 14021 is a statement or command of that order itself. Statutes, regulations and other instruments that the order cites keep whatever force they have independently of it, but they are not clauses of the order, so no independent command keeps any clause running after the revocation.","savings_check":"Savings were examined in the order's own text and in Executive Order 14148: section 2 contains no saving clause for the revoked orders, section 3(b) leaves existing actions to later review, and section 4 saves only statutory authority and Office of Management and Budget functions. The state is transferred_or_accrued for actions already taken, with no specific surviving action identified from held sources.","scope_check":"Section 2 of Executive Order 14148 revokes the order as a whole by number and by title, without limiting words and without excepting any clause, so the ending is not confined to part of the order. Section 4(a) of Executive Order 14148 states that nothing in it impairs the authority granted by law to an agency or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget; that preserves statutory authority and does not preserve any clause of this order."}

savings.reason: Section 3(b) of Executive Order 14148 directs the Director of the Domestic Policy Council and the Director of the National Economic Council to review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders, memoranda and proclamations listed in section 2 and to take necessary steps to rescind, replace or amend such actions as appropriate. Because rescission of actions already taken is left to later action, Federal actions already taken under Executive Order 14021 before 2025-01-20 were not themselves revoked by section 2 and stood until rescinded, replaced or amended individually. No held source identifies a particular surviving action or its later fate, so none is asserted.

source_notes.date_qualification: 2025-01-20: same signing date as EO 14148; the order of the two signings within that day is not established. The first-end date is the same under either instrument, so EO 14148 section 2 is recorded as the first-end actor and EO 14168 section 7(b) is recorded here as a concurrent express rescission.
source_notes.reason: Section 7(b) of Executive Order 14168 of 2025-01-20 (90 FR 8615) states that the requirements of that order supersede conflicting provisions in previous Executive Orders, including this order by number, and that "These Executive Orders are hereby rescinded". That is an express rescission of this order as a whole, with no effective-date wording, dated on signing, 2025-01-20. It is a second express rescission on the same day as Executive Order 14148 section 2 and gives no earlier date.
